nodes.description: Germline ETV6 missense and truncating variants yield stable mutant protein that is retained in the cytoplasm instead of the nucleus. Because ETV6 acts as a pointed-domain homodimer, mutant protein dimerises with and also retains wild-type ETV6 in the cytoplasm, a dominant-negative effect. For the recurrent central-domain variant p.Pro214Leu the mechanism is the de novo creation of an XPO1-dependent nuclear export signal; for ETS-domain variants nuclear import or retention is impaired by a mechanism that is less well defined.

biological_processes: XPO1-dependent nuclear export of ETV6 p.Pro214Leu
